System architecture

Responsibilities and boundaries in the system.

The boundaries matter more than the brands. Each layer owns a different kind of decision, which keeps persistent management from becoming unreviewed implementation.

DESIGN RULE

One layer, one job.

Persistence, project judgment, execution, and proof can collaborate closely without collapsing into one agent grading its own work.

01 · DIRECTION

Joe

Sets product direction, taste, scope changes, and consequential actions. Receives consolidated decisions rather than routine status requests.

  • Intent and priorities
  • One-way doors
  • Credentials and production actions
02 · PERSISTENCE

Hermes PM

Stays attached to one project, watches the tracker, notices worker outcomes, and starts the next authorized session.

  • Heartbeat and scheduling
  • Tracker continuity
  • Recovery and escalation
03 · ORCHESTRATION

DataCraft PM plugin

Turns accepted intent into outcome-sized work and keeps one accountable session responsible for integration and acceptance.

  • Dependency graph
  • Bounded worker briefs
  • Ship evidence
04 · EXECUTION + PROOF

Ringer

Dispatches the actual coding agents, runs their declared gates, and records receipts that PM can inspect.

  • Isolation and timeout
  • Executed checks
  • Logs, artifacts, and retry

Replaceable workers

The CLIs can change without changing the factory.

Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Grok Build are production lanes. Their cost and capability will change. The manager, work contract, verification gate, and durable record provide the stable architecture around them.
